description: Spotting, placing and mixing music under and around spoken word in documentaries, radio features and podcasts: where music enters and exits (downbeats, phrase ends, posts and buttons), ducking depth and timing, the 1–4 kHz carve (opendubstage carve), the music budget (how much of the narration may have music under it), song-relative levels, instrumentals instead of sung vocals under speech, checking generated underscores for hidden vocals, key-line handling and the ending ladder. Use when someone asks "where should the music come in", "how much should I duck", "the music fights the voice", "the song cuts off mid-phrase", "can I put this song under narration", is building a duck envelope or a sidechain, is designing an ending, or is choosing between a vocal track and an instrumental. Do NOT use for ambience beds or spot effects (ambience-and-sound-for-stills) or for chapter joins (scene-transitions).
